newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: High call rates keep Sri Lanka rupee strong.
newsitem.headline: High call rates keep Sri Lanka rupee strong.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee remained strong on the back of high call rates, as banks sold dollars to generate the local currency, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 56.52 to the dollar after opening at its previous closing level of 56.53.
"There was hardly any commercial demand for dollars, which came off as banks generated rupees," said a Sampath Bank dealer.
Overnight call money hit a high of 22 percent, before closing at 19, dealers said.
Call money is traditionally high at this time of the year, due to extra money leaving the system by way of bonus and fetival advance payments, dealers said.
"In addition, today was also sqauring up day which also made money a little tight," said the Sampath dealer.
